criteria.criterion: Queued edits are attempted in local creation order; each successful item is removed once, and the first failure leaves that item plus every later item queued in the same order.

criteria.criterion: A queued edit targeting a live tombstone is not applied; a target whose tombstone can no longer be proven within the 24-hour window is surfaced as a conflict and is not silently recreated.
criteria.evidence: Required verification: boundary cases immediately before, at, and after 24 hours.

criteria.criterion: A successfully replayed edit receives updated_at from models/record.py at apply time, and any client-provided updated_at cannot override it.
criteria.evidence: Required verification: a fixed model clock and a conflicting client timestamp.

decisions.rationale: The user explicitly selected the canonical model path; the remaining ordering, retry, tombstone, and timestamp risks are implementation constraints rather than alternate mechanics.

history.revision: When the app reconnects, synchronize the offline.edits queue by replaying each pending edit through the canonical models/record.py mutation path, in the queue's preserved local creation order. models/record.py remains the owner of updated_at stamping. A queue item is removed only after its record mutation succeeds; on failure, retain that item and all later items for retry. Reconnect reconciliation must honor any still-live server tombstone and must not silently recreate a record merely because its 24-hour tombstone has expired.

server/tombstones.py retains tombstones for 24 hours; PATH-002 is only a lexical offline.edits link. Behavior after expiry and the tombstone lookup API are absent.

summary.affected: Offline-created records and edits replayed after reconnect.
summary.possible_issue: Queued edits could bypass model normalization and timestamp stamping.
summary.prevention: Drain the queue only through models/record.py and verify every replayed mutation uses that path.
summary.trigger: The app reconnects with one or more pending queue items.

summary.affected: The failed queue item and all later locally created edits.
summary.possible_issue: Continuing after a failed edit or acknowledging too early can reorder dependent edits or lose local changes.
summary.prevention: Process sequentially, acknowledge after success, and stop while retaining the failed suffix.
summary.trigger: A record mutation fails partway through reconnect synchronization.

summary.affected: Records deleted while a client remains offline.
summary.possible_issue: An offline edit can resurrect a server-deleted record, especially after its tombstone expires.
summary.prevention: Reject live-tombstone conflicts and surface expired-window conflicts instead of silently recreating records.
summary.trigger: A queued edit targets a record with a live or already-expired deletion tombstone.

summary.possible_issue: Using a client-supplied or queue-time timestamp can violate model ownership and alter conflict resolution.
summary.prevention: Have models/record.py stamp updated_at when the replay mutation is applied and test that client timestamps do not override it.
summary.trigger: A queued edit is replayed after reconnect.
